subject: Banking
title: Apple Pay and Tokenization
description: A short lesson to help you apply Apple Pay and Tokenization.

hook.text: Apple Pay never shares your real card number with the merchant. A unique token replaces it for every transaction.

buildup.text: When you add a card to Apple Pay, your bank creates a Device Account Number stored in the phone's secure chip.

discovery.text: Each payment generates a one-time dynamic security code. Even if a hacker intercepts it, the token cannot be reused.

twist.text: Apple charges banks 0.15% per transaction for this service.

climax.text: Apple became a payment company without being a bank. It charges rent on the most secure checkout experience.

punchline.text: Your real card number is never shared. Apple charges banks for the safety.

quiz.question: How does Apple Pay protect card information?
options: Replacing the real card number with a unique token for each transaction

details.summary: Apple Pay replaces your real card number with a unique device-specific token during transactions, so the merchant never sees your actual card details, dramatically reducing the risk of card data theft.
details.whyItMatters: Tokenization is the most significant anti-fraud innovation in payment security since chip cards. It makes stolen transaction data useless to thieves because tokens cannot be reused elsewhere.
takeaways: A device-specific token replaces your real card number at the point of sale
Merchants never receive or store your actual card details
Each transaction uses a unique one-time cryptogram for verification

faq.question: Is Apple Pay safer than using a physical credit card?
faq.answer: Yes. A physical card exposes your real number to every merchant and can be skimmed. Apple Pay never shares your actual card number, and biometric authentication adds a second layer of security that physical cards lack.

faq.question: What happens to Apple Pay if your phone is stolen?
faq.answer: You can remotely disable Apple Pay through Find My iPhone without canceling your physical cards. The tokens on the stolen device become useless, and your actual card numbers were never stored on the device.
